# Skelcrew

> Skelcrew is your own team of coding agents, working while you're away. You brief a lead agent in the harness you already use. It writes the tasks and hands each one to a builder, and a fresh reviewer on another model checks every pull request. The team works on your own server, so you can close the laptop. You decide what merges. Open source.

Status: early. Earlier versions ran tasks to pull requests through phases, roles and gates defined as files; the current rewrite, started in November 2026, organises agents as a small team instead. No public release yet. Launching November 2026. Sign up for launch news at https://skelcrew.dev

## The team

- The lead: your agent, in your harness, on your server. It turns what you say into tasks (GitHub issues) and starts a thread on each.
- Builders: one per task, each in its own clone, branch and sandbox. A builder stays on the thread until the pull request merges.
- Reviewers: a fresh one every round, on another model than the builder (Codex by default), looking for what the builder missed.
- You: say what you want, answer questions, and decide what merges.

## What you hand off

- Task to merged pull request, while you're away
- Many tasks at once, across repositories
- Every pull request reviewed by a fresh agent; the verdict is a GitHub review and a `skelcrew/review` status check
- CI failures and pull request comments wake the builder again
- It asks you only when it needs you: a builder's question, a review that won't settle, or a pull request that is approved and green
- You decide what merges

## Open and adaptable, by design

Being open and adaptable is a core design principle. Harnesses, models, forges and servers each sit behind one small seam.

- Harnesses and models: Claude Code and Codex today, builder on one and reviewer on the other. Built to take any harness and any model, on the subscriptions you already pay for. Skelcrew never resells model usage.
- Forges: GitHub today. GitLab, Forgejo and Codeberg can plug in through the same seam.
- Servers: the demo runs on a Sprite on Fly.io, which sleeps when there's no work. Any Linux machine that stays on works, reached over SSH.
- Isolation: a sandbox per agent; your checkouts are never touched; your home folder and credentials are hidden; agents never see your tokens.
- Free and open source.

## Settings example

```yaml
# ~/.config/skelcrew/config.yaml
harness: claude
builder:  { model: opus }
reviewer: { harness: codex }
max_rounds: 3

# skelcrew.yaml in a repository
setup: [bun install]
test: [bun test]
```
